market_summary: Tariff-sensitive tape was flat on Aug 29: SPY 771.10, XLI 178.80, XLB 53.23, XME 123.00, SLX 109.73, ITA 234.26, with FXI 35.24/MCHI 54.90 soft on China overhang and CAD 1.3901 steady ahead of Sep 8 retaliation. Industrials and materials diverging — XLI defense capex bid vs XLB commodity pricing power — as effective tariff rate sits at 9.6% (+7.6 pp).

top_story.headline: USTR's 60-Economy Section 301 Tariffs (10–12.5%) Take Effect — Replaces Struck-Down IEEPA Regime
top_story.why_it_matters: The July 28 Federal Register notice rebuilds the tariff wall struck down 6-3 in March (Learning Resources v. Trump) on the sturdier Section 301 foundation, imposing 10% or 12.5% (net of MFN) on 60 partners. It sets the legal floor for every subsequent stack — Canada 50% Section 338, China 70% chips — and creates the TRQ carve-outs that will decide who keeps margin.

themes.title: Canada Flashpoint — 5% of Imports, 100% of Politics
themes.synthesis: Washington's 50% Section 338 on ~5% of Canada imports and Ottawa's Sep 8 dollar-for-dollar retaliation are surgically narrow but hit autos Jan 1, 2027 at 50% and risk USMCA withdrawal optics; Russell notes U.S. growth impact muted, Canada hit harder due to export concentration.

themes.title: China Stack Nears Legal Ceiling — 70% for Chips
themes.synthesis: Pending 7.5% overcapacity tariff on 16 partners/22 sectors would bring China chips to 70% (50% IP + 12.5% forced labor + 7.5%) — exactly the 20% second-term replacement ceiling set in Busan/Beijing — leaving no room for broader hikes before the Sep 24 summit and Nov 10 truce expiry.

themes.title: Earnings Flattered, Margins Squeezed — Refund vs Pass-Through
themes.synthesis: $100B of $168B IEEPA duties refunded by July 31 (Walmart $2.9B) is a one-time Q3 earnings windfall, while 82% of manufacturers now pass costs through (from 44% in 2025) — a Yale 9.6% effective rate that compresses metal fabricators regardless of top-line tariff narratives.

outlook: Watch USTR Federal Register before Sep 24 for overcapacity final rate, Canada retaliation Sep 8 and USMCA rhetoric, and XLI-XLB spread — if XLB leads, commodity-cycle tariffs dominate margins; if XLI leads, capex resilience offsets duties into Q4 earnings.
